title: Power Pages: enhanced authorisation maps web roles and site users to Dataverse security
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, site enablement path, licensing and authorization behaviour are supported. The Site table reference confirms the PATCH operation and enhancedauthorization field despite the automatic pre-check. A minor checklist/table mismatch remains for permission and auditing controls.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Permission evaluation shifts directly to Dataverse based on the site user's roles.
claims.quote: When you enable enhanced authorization, permission evaluation shifts directly to Dataverse. In this model, Dataverse evaluates permissions based on the site user's roles

claims.claim: Dataverse returns only records that the site user is permitted to access.
claims.quote: Dataverse evaluates permissions based on the site user's roles and returns only the records the user is allowed to access.

claims.claim: The standard model checks permissions in Power Pages after retrieval using an elevated application user.
claims.quote: In the standard authorization model, Power Pages evaluates table and record permissions after data retrieval from Dataverse by using the Power Pages application user that runs with elevated privilege

claims.claim: Enhanced authorization removes the extra permission-checking layer in Power Pages.
claims.quote: This change removes the extra permission checking layer at Power Pages and ensures alignment with Dataverse's native security model.

claims.claim: Dataverse operations execute on behalf of the site user through impersonation rather than the application user.
claims.quote: Dataverse operations execute on behalf of the site user by using impersonation rather than the application user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
